gift_h2: Bangle designs to compare before choosing a size
gift_blurb: A measurement is only the starting point. Compare the inner shape, width, hinge, clasp, and profile of the design you want. These BlueStone bangles show why a slim round piece, an oval hinged form, and a broader decorative bangle can feel different even when their listed dimensions look close. Use each product page and fitting guidance for the final choice.
conclusion_html: The safest bangle size decision starts with the right measurement for the right construction. Copy the inner diameter of a comfortable bangle when possible. Otherwise, measure the widest part of your grouped hand for a closed design, compare the result with the chart, and confirm the product-specific instructions. If the reading is uncertain or the design is wide, oval, hinged, or difficult to alter, a professional fitting is worth the extra step.

tail_h2: How to use this bangle size guide before buying
how_to_html: Write down three things before you shop: the measurement, the method used, and the bangle construction you plan to buy. Compare all three with the exact product page. If the values disagree, you are between sizes, or the design is wide or oval, pause the order and ask for a professional fitting.
faq_h2: Frequently Asked Questions about Bangle Size

section_leads.Bangle size chart in mm, cm and inches: The BlueStone Bangle Measuring Guide and the Gem and Jewellery Skill Council of India retail training handbook use the standard inner-diameter progression below. Values are rounded for practical measuring, so retain millimetres until you have chosen the closest size.
section_leads.How to measure bangle size using a bangl: This is usually the simplest method because it copies a fit that already works. Accuracy depends on choosing a comfortable, undistorted reference and measuring only the clear opening through its true centre.
section_leads.How to measure your hand for bangle size: Use the hand method when you do not own a suitable reference bangle. The measurement must represent the widest shape the closed bangle will pass over, not the narrower wrist where it eventually rests.
section_leads.Closed, openable and adjustable bangle s: Bangle construction changes the fitting route. Closed designs slide over the hand, while hinged and adjustable designs can open closer to the wrist. Match the method to the mechanism before converting a number.
section_leads.How should a correctly sized bangle fit?: The correct fit is secure and wearable, not merely possible to put on. Check the entire sequence from passing the hand to moving at the wrist and removing the bangle again.
section_leads.Common bangle size mistakes and how to f: Most wrong-size orders begin with a small measurement error or the wrong reference point. A second reading and a construction check can prevent a centimetre, diameter, or wrist measurement from being applied to the wrong product.
section_leads.Choosing a size for wide, oval and stack: A size label cannot describe every contact point. Width, profile, internal shape, hinges, stones, and neighbouring bangles all change how a design feels during wear.
section_leads.Bangle size buying checklist for online: Turn the chart into a safe purchase by recording what you measured and comparing it with the exact listing. Never let a familiar size label replace the product dimensions and construction notes.
section_leads.When to visit a BlueStone store for a fi: Home measurement is useful, but it should not become a guess when the values conflict or the design is complex. A store fitting lets you compare the actual construction, movement, and hand clearance.
section_leads.Fact sources for this bangle size guide: The measurement methods and chart values were checked against the BlueStone Bangle Measuring Guide, the Gem and Jewellery Skill Council of India training handbook, and BlueStone's existing measurement explainer.
